data.name: Camilla
data.gender_notes: Camilla is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word ‘camilla’, which means ‘younger sister’ or ‘attendant maid’. In Christian tradition, it is associated with the names of two saints: Saint Camilla de'Rossano and Saint Camilla of Capua. The name Camilla carries the meaning “Younger Sister” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Camilla usually hope their child will grow to embody younger sister and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Camilla belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Younger Sister.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Camilla total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Καμίλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Καμίλα είναι το όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'κοντοκράτος' ή 'φυτό'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα αυτό, αλλά συνδέεται με ονόματα φυτών και λουλουδιών που αναφέρονται στα Ιερά Κείμενα. Το όνομα Καμίλα χρησιμοποιείται ευρέως ανάμεσα στους Χριστιανούς και θεωρείται ένα όμορφο και χαρισματικό όνομα.

in_english.name: Camilla

in_english.long_meaning: The name Camilla originates from Latin, meaning 'young ceremonial attendant' or 'plant'. It does not have a direct biblical reference but is associated with nature and growth, themes present in Christian scripture. Historically, Camilla was a Roman name borne by a legendary queen, and it has been adopted in Christian traditions, symbolizing virtues like modesty and dedication. The name is popular across various Christian cultures, representing a blend of classical heritage and spiritual values.

data.cultural_impact: The name Camilla is rich in history and culture. It has its roots in Latin origin and was used as a name for attendant maids or younger sisters. In ancient mythology, Camilla was also the name of an Amazon queen known for her warrior skills and independence. This name has been popular in various cultures and centuries, from ancient Rome to medieval Europe and beyond. Today, Camilla is a name that evokes a sense of strength, uniqueness, and grace.
data.spiritual_significance: Camilla is a name that carries deep spiritual significance for Christians. It is associated with two holy saints: Saint Camilla de'Rossano and Saint Camilla of Capua. Both saints were remarkable women of faith who lived their lives dedicated to God. Saint Camilla de'Rossano was a hermit who lived in solitude and devoted herself to prayer and penance. Her courage and unwavering faith earned her the title "The Lady of the Castle." Saint Camilla of Capua, on the other hand, was a very young nun who died of natural causes at the young age of 18. Her mystical experiences and deep devotion to God continue to inspire and awe people today. Camilla is a name that symbolizes purity, faith, and courage in the face of adversity, making it a beautiful and meaningful name for a Christian girl.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Camilla: Devoted to the Roman goddess Diana, symbolizing agility, fertility, and protection in hunting and childbirth. In Christianity, it represents the virtuous woman, strong in faith and nurturing in love.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Camilla, the warrior queen of the Volscians, is a legendary figure in Roman mythology. The name Camilla carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
